issues: LOAD-BEARING THESIS INTERROGATED AND HELD. The thesis is: 39:34-35 is the accounting mechanism behind 39:53 — the worst is covered (li-yukaffira, Form II 'cover'), and the wage is computed from the best line in the file (bi-aḥsani), with the same record read from opposite ends for the two destinies. Every component checks out independently: the purpose-lām is corpus-tagged PRP; yukaffira is Form II of kfr; aswaʾ is exactly 2× and is the denier's line at 41:27; 39:53 sits 18 ayahs later; and al-Ṭabarī states the دون أسوئها ('not by the worst of it') mechanism explicitly in the file's own tafsir report. Unlike 21:76-77, there is no false proposition holding this file up.

THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE MISS — the file never mentions 29:7, which is the actual one-word twin it claims to have found. 29:7 reads وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَحْسَنَ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ; 41:27 reads وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَسْوَأَ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ. These two are IDENTICAL except for the single word أَحْسَنَ / أَسْوَأَ — same emphatic verb la-najziyannahum, no bāʾ, no ajrahum. That is the pair where 'the slot where they finally part is a single word' is literally true. And 29:7 opens with لَنُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ — the same kaffara-ʿan covering move as 39:35. 29:7 is a better exemplar of the file's own thesis than the pair it chose, and it goes unnamed. This does not falsify the argument; it means the file overclaimed on the wrong pair while the exact claim it wanted was available one verse away.

IKHTILĀF PRESENT IN THE FILE'S OWN REPORT AND UNACKNOWLEDGED. al-Jalalayn at 39:35 says أسْوَأ وأَحْسَن بِمَعْنى السَّيِّئ والحَسَن — 'aswaʾ and aḥsan here carry the meaning of the bad and the good', i.e. he reads both elatives as standing for the plain positive degree, NOT as superlatives. The file leans its whole reading on superlative force ('the superlative worst', 'his record is read from the bottom', 'the best line in his file'). al-Ṭabarī's دون أسوئها supports the file's direction, so the reading is defensible and I am not calling the thesis false — but a named commentator in the supplied report directly qualifies the file's central grammatical move, and the file does not say so. This is the same class of omission the tadabbur methodology exists to prevent.

TAFSIR REPORT DEFECT PRESENT (both known modes, milder than file 1). The Ibn Kathīr block is byte-identical under 39:34 and 39:35 and quotes ayahs 32-35 as a run. The al-Ṭabarī block under the 39:34 heading is actually the 39:33 commentary (heading text: ﴿وَالَّذِي جَاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ … (٣٣) لَهُمْ مَا يَشَاءُونَ … (٣٤)﴾) and its body discusses only 39:33 before truncating. MITIGATING: the file cites Ibn Kathīr nowhere, and its one al-Ṭabarī citation draws from the 39:35 block, which is correctly keyed. No false attribution resulted.
